S No directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  13.06.2024 WPCRL No. 624 of 2024  Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1.
Ms. Shruti Joshi, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. V.K. Jemini, learned Deputy Advocate General, along with Mr. Akshay Latwal, learned Brief Holder for the State.

2. By the instant petition, the petitioner is praying for quashing of FIR No. 0007 of 2024 dated 02.06.2024, wherein the present petitioner has been implicated for the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC, P.S. Lansdowne, District Pauri Garhwal.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner, by profession is a contractor and he provide the labourers to the other contractors and engaged the parents of the complainant in the construction sites.

4. The impugned FIR was lodged by the informant/complainant with the allegations that she is the citizen of Nepal and on 01.06.2024 at about 7 p.m., the present petitioner outraged the modesty of the complainant, consequently on her complaint, the impugned FIR was registered for the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that it is absolutely a false allegation, which has been alleged in the impugned FIR and the petitioner is innocent.
Furthermore, she submits that even as per the allegation, no cognizable offence is made out against the petitioner for the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated and the impugned FIR is nothing but a pressure tactics and the petitioner has no previous criminal history.

Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the petitioner is ready to undertake that he will cooperate with the investigation; however, without collecting any cogent evidence, the petitioner may not be arrested otherwise it would amount to miscarriage of justice.

7. It is also contended that without investigating the entire matter, the Investigating Officer is threatening the petitioner to arrest, which is in violation of the fundamental rights of the petitioner.

1 8.
No doubt, the allegation as alleged in the impugned FIR requires investigation and at this stage no opinion can be given on the merit of the case.
Certainly, the matter requires scrutiny and deliberation for which the counter affidavit is necessary.

9. Mr. V.K. Jemini, learned Deputy Advocate General accepts notice for respondent Nos. 1 & 2.
10.

Issue notice to respondent No. 3.
11. Let the respondents may file counter affidavit within four weeks.
Two weeks' time, thereafter is also granted to the petitioner to file rejoinder affidavit.

12. List this matter in the week commencing 22nd July, 2024.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 13.06.2024 Mahinder/
